sourceTitle: Chloroplast genome engineering: Recent advances, pathways towards commercialization and future directions.
sourceAbstract: Chloroplasts are ideal biofactories because thousands of transgene copies integrated into each plant cell to produce high levels of recombinant proteins and enzymes. Because chloroplast genomes are predominantly maternally inherited, transgenes are generally not transmitted via pollen. Nuclear genome engineering ushered in the GMO revolution for crop protection that mostly required lower levels of transgene expression. Higher level expression and biosafety through gene containment facilitate new applications of GM crops, including production of high-value biopharmaceuticals and enzymes. This review focuses on recent advances in this field, including the first FDA approval of biopharmaceuticals made in plant cells for evaluation in human clinical trials, topical or oral drug delivery, marker free edible plants by removal of antibiotic resistance genes and novel post-translational modifications required to produce functional human proteins. In addition, new tools are discussed to improve DNA delivery, vector free assembly, episomal or integration methods, enhancement of transgene expression through optimization of regulatory sequences, codons, targeted genome editing and other innovations in biomanufacturing. Topical drug delivery using plant cells incorporated into chewing gums to control oral viruses, pathogenic bacteria, or yeast and oral drug delivery with therapeutic proteins made in plant cells to treat diabetes, obesity and cardiopulmonary diseases currently advanced to human clinical trials are discussed. In addition, high-value industrial enzymes for launching new products or to confer valuable agronomic traits or enhance photosynthesis are discussed. Future perspectives section provides examples of biotechnology products anticipated to be launched in the next 3-5 years, with opportunities and anticipated challenges.
titleZh: 叶绿体基因组工程：近期进展、商业化路径与未来方向
abstractZh: 叶绿体是理想的生物工厂，因为每个植物细胞中可整合数千个转基因拷贝，从而高水平生产重组蛋白和酶。由于叶绿体基因组主要通过母系遗传，转基因通常不会经花粉传播。核基因组工程开启了以作物保护为目标的转基因生物（GMO）革命，而这类应用大多只需要较低的转基因表达水平。更高水平的表达，以及通过限制基因扩散而实现的生物安全性，有助于拓展转基因作物的新应用，包括生产高价值生物药和酶。本综述重点介绍该领域的近期进展，包括植物细胞制备的生物药首次获美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准开展人体临床试验评估、局部或口服给药、通过去除抗生素抗性基因获得不含筛选标记的可食用植物，以及产生有功能的人源蛋白所需的新型翻译后修饰。此外，文章讨论了改善DNA递送、无载体组装、游离型或整合型方法的新工具，通过优化调控序列和密码子增强转基因表达的方法、靶向基因组编辑，以及生物制造中的其他创新。文中还讨论了利用含植物细胞的口香糖进行局部给药、以控制口腔病毒、致病细菌或酵母，以及使用植物细胞制得的治疗性蛋白进行口服给药、以治疗糖尿病、肥胖和心肺疾病的策略；这些策略目前已推进至人体临床试验。文章还讨论了用于推出新产品、赋予有价值的农艺性状或增强光合作用的高价值工业酶。未来展望部分列举了有望在未来3—5年推出的生物技术产品，并讨论了相关机遇与预期挑战。

sourceTitle: Cell culture tightrope: Balancing amino acids and dipeptides to optimize media formulation and biomanufacturing performance.
sourceAbstract: High-quality cell culture media remain central to mammalian bioprocessing as industry produces increasingly complex molecules at higher cell densities under intensified processing conditions. Amino acids represent a critical class of media components, serving as building blocks for endogenous and recombinant proteins and also as key regulators of cellular metabolism. This requires delivery of amino acids at concentrations that challenge their stability and solubility limits. This review provides an overview of amino acid roles in cell culture and how to choose their optimal levels in media formulations, with a focus on Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. Omics-assisted medium development strategies are described to characterize amino acid metabolism and minimize metabolic inefficiencies arising from amino acid degradation. Additionally, genetic engineering approaches aimed at introducing amino acid auxotrophies or removing metabolic bottlenecks are discussed as complementary strategies to improve cell culture performance. Understanding the physicochemical limitations associated with amino acid solubility becomes increasingly important in concentrated media formulations. Emerging in silico thermodynamic models that capture interactions between amino acids and other media components are highlighted as valuable tools for predicting solubility limits and guiding rational media formulation strategies. Dipeptides represent an increasingly attractive alternative to free amino acids due to improved solubility, stability, and process-enhancing properties. Consequently, this review summarizes key dipeptides, current knowledge of their uptake and metabolism, and the amino acid and dipeptide transporters and cleavage enzymes. Finally, the review emphasizes the importance of smart media design by integrating experiments with modeling approaches to enable efficient, robust, and sustainable biomanufacturing processes.
titleZh: 细胞培养中的精细平衡：调配氨基酸与二肽，优化培养基配方及生物制造性能
abstractZh: 随着工业界在强化工艺条件下，以更高细胞密度生产日益复杂的分子，高质量细胞培养基仍然是哺乳动物生物加工的核心。氨基酸是一类关键培养基组分，既是内源蛋白和重组蛋白的构建单元，也是细胞代谢的重要调节因子。因此，氨基酸的供给浓度会对其稳定性和溶解度极限构成挑战。本综述概述氨基酸在细胞培养中的作用，以及如何为培养基配方选择最佳氨基酸水平，重点关注中国仓鼠卵巢（CHO）细胞。文章介绍了组学辅助的培养基开发策略，用于表征氨基酸代谢，并尽量减少由氨基酸降解引起的代谢低效。此外，综述讨论了旨在引入氨基酸营养缺陷或解除代谢瓶颈的遗传工程方法，将其作为改善细胞培养性能的互补策略。在浓缩培养基配方中，理解氨基酸溶解度相关的理化限制变得日益重要。新兴的计算热力学模型能够描述氨基酸与其他培养基组分之间的相互作用，文章强调了其作为预测溶解度极限、指导理性培养基配方设计的有价值工具的作用。由于溶解度、稳定性以及促进工艺表现的性质有所改善，二肽正日益成为颇具吸引力的游离氨基酸替代选择。因此，本综述总结了关键二肽、目前关于其摄取和代谢的认识，以及氨基酸和二肽的转运蛋白与切割酶。最后，综述强调，将实验与建模方法相结合开展智能培养基设计，对于实现高效、稳健且可持续的生物制造过程具有重要意义。
